thread.title: Fitbit: Boom Times Ahead - Fitbit, Inc. (NYSE:FIT)

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Fitbit: Boom Times Ahead - Fitbit, Inc. (NYSE:FIT)
text:
The market forecasts are starting to support my investment thesis that Fitbit ( FIT ) is poised for a period of strong growth. The stock has recently held around $5 in the massive tech-led selloff due to new devices and a cheap valuation. The market potential in smartwatches catering to medical issues is big catalyst for the market and the stock.
Image Source: Fitbit website
Market Research Gartner forecasts a surge in wearables devices by 2022. Smartwatches are expected to a be a leading source of growth with demand more than doubling from 53 million units this year to 115 million in 2022. The research firm even forecasts wristbands to grow by about 12 million annual units in the next four years.
The hottest sectors from this point are in head-mounted displays and ear-worn, neither of which Fitbit expects to participate. The key though is that Gartner had previously predicted that large health systems and enterprises will quickly move into full-scale rollouts of digital health programs. These programs will include wearable devices, smartwatch or fitness tracker, that monitors health and sends danger signals back into an integrated system.
Per Gartner researcher Christy Pettey in her report on connected health monitoring:
The next wave of wearable health market growth will come from integrated systems that are able to sense danger signals.
Despite all the woes at Fitbit over the last couple of years, the company still remains the third largest wearables company by shipment volumes. The company is the second largest smartwatch vendor and IDC sees their work in sleep quality as a differentiator.
Otherwise, IDC sees Fitbit having a future in medical devices that Gartner predicts as one of the growth drivers in the medical market through 2022. The market appears wide open based on market research with a determining factor in the success of the categories based on whether Apple ( AAPL ) and Fitbit can successfully implement functions in future devices with FDA clearance demanded by either consumers or enterprise health plans.
Valuation Reminder Based on the forecasts, no doubt should exists that Fitbit is plugged into a great market opportunity over the next few years. The stock shouldn't trade at levels anywhere close to $5, much less below that key threshold.
A lot of investors like to brush off the comparison to Garmin ( GRMN ), but the potential for Fitbit to duplicate the success path of Garmin is undeniable. Considering that Fitbit has successfully fended off Garmin in the fitness category should provide another indication that the stocks should traded closer to similar EV/S multiples.
FIT EV to Revenues (Forward) data by YCharts
Yes, Garmin is a highly profitable company due to sales in aviation and outdoor categories on top of fitness, but Fitbit isn't that far away to discredit the stock with 1/10th the multiple. Besides, Fitbit has the balance sheet to support ongoing investments in product development to capture the growth opportunity in smartwatches and medical devices with FDA clearance.
Of course, Fitbit won't capture the same multiple until the company becomes profitable, but in no way should the stock trade at such a low EV/S multiple. Just a simple 1x multiple with '19 sales of $1.57 billion and a cash balance of over $620 million places the stock at $9.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that both Gartner and IDC place Fitbit in a good position to capture a growing market over the next few years. The big bonus to investors is that the stock below $5 isn't even reflective of the current turnaround at the company, not to mention the upside potential from the bonanza of a medical device shift.
The stock remains a bargain anywhere around $5.
